meta.description: Comprehensive Dutch-English cycling vocabulary. Covers all terms used in questions plus many additional terms a cyclist will encounter on Dutch roads.

terms.context: Used on signs and in traffic rules to indicate who goes first.
Appears on triangular yield signs. Verlenen means to grant — you are granting priority to others.
A road marked with a yellow diamond sign where you have priority at every junction.
White triangles painted on the road. Pointing at you = you yield.
As in right-before-left — rechts heeft voorrang.
Direction. Traffic from your left must yield to you at unmarked junctions.
A priority road that bends — the priority follows the bend, not the straight road.
On rectangular white signs with blue border — marks an optional cycle path.
A road where cyclists are primary users. Cars are guests and may not overtake.
Rijwiel is an older Dutch word for bicycle. Same as fietspad in practice.
Seen on signs and sub-signs. Plural: fietsers.
A warning to car drivers that cyclists may cross the road ahead.
Seen on fietsstraat signs. Means cars must defer to cyclists on this road.
A motorised two-wheeler. Some cycle paths allow bromfietsen, others don't.
A moped limited to 25km/h. Allowed on most cycle paths.
Legally classified as a moped. Must ride on the road, not cycle paths. Helmet required.
The most common word on Dutch prohibition signs.
Seen on round red signs with a white bar. No vehicles may enter.
Applies to all road users including cyclists, not just cars.

terms.translation: No driving through / don't block the junction
terms.context: Similar to 'don't block the box' in English.
A road that is gesloten is closed to traffic.
Often seen on temporary road closure signs.
The road operates in one direction only.
Means the road doesn't connect through to anywhere.
Cycling on the stoep is illegal.
The key sub-sign word. Uitgezonderd fietsers = except cyclists.
Residents, deliveries, and visitors to a specific address may enter.
Only people with a permit may enter or park here.
A general warning seen on signs and heard from other road users.
Seen on triangular warning signs.
Often seen near schools, residential zones, or construction.
Warning that the road or cycle path surface is in bad condition.
Common in 30km/h zones and residential areas.
Warning that the road or path gets narrower ahead.
The general word for road.
The road surface itself, as opposed to the shoulder or pavement.
A single traffic lane within a road.
The strip of grass or gravel beside the road.
Any point where two or more roads meet.
Circular junction. Dutch roundabouts often have separate cycle rings.
A designated place to cross the road.
The wonderfully long Dutch word for a zebra crossing.
Pedestrians have priority, speed limit is walking pace.
The speed limit on most Dutch city streets. Applies to cyclists too.
The road doesn't connect through.
Traffic moves in both directions.
Crossing a road or junction.
Passing another road user.
Rechts afslaan = turn right. Links afslaan = turn left.
Continue in the same direction.
Slow down or stop.
Get off your bicycle. Required in some pedestrian zones.
Use your bell to signal your presence.
A designated place to park your bicycle, often underground at train stations.
Generic term for any traffic signal.
The everyday word for traffic light.
Any road sign.
Painted lines, arrows, or symbols on the road surface.
An underpass for cyclists, common at busy junctions and railway crossings.
An overpass for cyclists.
Usually off-limits to cyclists unless specifically signed.
Cross at 90 degrees to avoid getting your wheel trapped.
A financial penalty for a traffic violation.
The physical or digital notice of a fine.
Dutch police actively enforce cycling laws, especially in city centres.
Traffic enforcement, often done by municipal officers as well as police.
Verplicht fietspad = mandatory cycle path.
Not required for regular cycling, but relevant for speed pedelec riders.
In Dutch law, motorists bear a higher liability burden in collisions with cyclists.
Expect rain regularly. Most Dutch cyclists just keep riding.
The Netherlands is flat and windy. Headwinds are a daily reality.
Warning sign for ice, wet leaves, or other slippery surfaces.
Extremely dangerous for cyclists. Check conditions on cold mornings.
You'll become very familiar with this word during your first Dutch winter.
